note: Lifted semantic model, TEAS side. Concepts decompose the same network into per-layer networks. tunnel-termination-point is the false-cognate trap: it shares the '-termination-point' shape with the TAPI link-termination-point but originates a tunnel (a trail head), which its relations and instances make plain even when the gloss is withheld.

concepts.label: te-node
concepts.gloss: a traffic-engineering node in a per-layer network
concepts.example: ROADM R1 in the OTN layer

concepts.label: termination-point
concepts.gloss: a termination point where a te-link terminates on a node

concepts.label: supporting-tp
concepts.gloss: the supporting relationship of a tp on a server-layer tp
concepts.example: an OTN tp supported by an optical tp at R1
instances: OTN tp over optical tp at R1

concepts.label: tunnel-termination-point
concepts.gloss: the point at which a te-tunnel originates or terminates, i.e. a trail head
concepts.example: the head of the A1-A3 tunnel at A1

concepts.label: te-tunnel
concepts.gloss: an end-to-end traffic-engineered tunnel realising a service

concepts.label: otn-label
concepts.gloss: the OTN label expressing tributary-slot multiplexing structure
concepts.example: the tributary slots carrying ODU2 in an OTU4

concepts.label: connectivity-matrix
concepts.gloss: the matrix of permitted internal connectivity within a node

concepts.label: te-link
concepts.gloss: a traffic-engineering link between nodes in a layer network

concepts.label: tunnel-connection-endpoint
concepts.gloss: an endpoint of a tunnel connection within a node
concepts.example: the connection endpoint for the A1-A3 tunnel on R1
